clue.text: A more loudly-played tune produces concern …

parts.note: FF is fortissimo in music, a direction to play very loudly
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a melody played at greater volume causes worry.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the clue on into 5 across, but each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or business, something that is one's concern.

clue.text: Full of enthusiasm, given one's cards

explanation.surface: An eager worker is sacked anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, being given one's cards means being dismissed from a job (the employment cards were handed back).
explanation.definitionFit: Fired up means excited; fired also means sacked from a job.

clue.text: Deviation from Canberra's reform Aussie finally supports

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits below it
reform means the letters of the city are formed again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Aussie

explanation.surface: A political shake-up in the Australian capital is backed by a voter, causing a departure from the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges CANBERRA into ABERRANC; 'finally' takes E from Aussie, which 'supports' places beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrance is a straying from what is normal or expected.

clue.text: Figures broken rib will restrict man? Not entirely

indicators.note: will restrict means the shuffled rib letters close round the shortened word for man
broken means the letters of rib are smashed into a new order
not entirely means the last letter of the word for man is cut off

parts.note: homo is Latin for man, as in the genus Homo

explanation.surface: An X-ray shows a broken rib that will hold a man back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' scrambles the bone's letters so they can open round the shortened Latin word, which 'Not entirely' trims by its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi are geometric shapes, plural of rhombus, a four-sided figure with equal sides.

clue.text: … in view of what programme tells us

explanation.surface: A broadcast tells us what is in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis continues 1 across's surface; 'of' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Visible means displayed on the screen, and a TV programme shows what is on the screen.

clue.text: In brilliant form, perhaps, most excellent among original vital intake

definitions.text: In brilliant form, perhaps, most excellent

parts.note: among can mean of the, as in one among the best being one of the best
first means original or earliest
water is the drink every body needs to survive

explanation.surface: A brilliant performer is at the top of his game while taking in essential fluids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brilliant' points to diamonds, whose clarity is graded by water; the finest are of the first water.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds of the highest clarity are graded first water, so the phrase means top quality.

clue.text: Right to interrupt female with desire to be always nagging

indicators.note: to interrupt means the letter for right breaks into the word for female

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: A woman who wants things her way keeps on complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrewish woman is bad-tempered and scolding, constantly carping.

clue.text: Out of practice, manage without new pen

indicators.note: without means the letter for new is taken away

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Someone rusty at writing tries to cope without a new pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Skills that have not been used lately become stale and rough.

clue.text: Cook pie and make better one for a gourmet

indicators.note: cook means the letters of pie are treated loosely and rearranged

parts.note: to cure is to make better
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: A chef bakes a pie and improves it for a food lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is someone devoted to fine food and drink.

clue.text: Drink knocked back during soccer? Spoils 25 one's aim as attacker 26

indicators.note: during places the drink inside the word for soccer

parts.note: footer is a British slang name for football or soccer

indicators.note: knocked back means the word for the drink is turned round, as a drink is downed

parts.note: beer is a drink

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a pint during a football match, while a striker aims at goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses the drink, as a drink is downed, and it sits just after the first letter of the slang word for soccer. The numbers 25 and 26 are stray marks in the scanned clue and play no part.
explanation.definitionFit: A freebooter is a pirate or plunderer, whose goal in raiding is loot.

clue.text: Fit part of a deck

explanation.surface: A card player checks which cards match.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit is to be fitting; a suit is one of the four sets in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Trouble taken with half- 28 hearted mob that may be greatly admired

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two middle letters of the word for mob is dropped, leaving half its heart

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A crowd with little spirit has caused trouble, yet still wins admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBLE has BB at its heart; half-hearted drops one B, leaving RABLE. The '28' is a stray mark in the scanned clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means lovable, worthy of being doted on.

clue.text: Unconventional exit

explanation.surface: An odd way of leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Way-out is slang for weird or unorthodox; a way out is a door for leaving.

clue.text: Son is able to make short 2 work of studies

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: A clever boy gets through his homework quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: To scan is to read through rapidly, getting studies done quickly. The '2' is a stray mark in the scanned clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanning a text means glancing over it quickly instead of reading closely.

clue.text: Hit Leo for one in the bar after a round's finished

definitions.text: the bar after a round's finished

parts.note: to club is to hit
Leo is one of the twelve houses or signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A golfer strikes a partner named Leo in the bar after the game.
explanation.walkthrough: A round here is a round of golf: golfers drink in the club building afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club's main building, with its bar, is where players gather after playing.

clue.text: Wearing a suit, to a 3 greater extent

explanation.surface: A man in a smart outfit looks even better.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a hand or contract can be in spades, one of the four card suits. The '3' is a stray mark in the scanned clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is a card suit; colloquially, in spades means in abundance or to a high degree.

clue.text: Kind like Sam or Tom

explanation.surface: A kindly man resembles two friends called Sam and Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam personifies the USA; Uncle Tom is the hero of Uncle Tom's Cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: Avuncular means benevolent, like a kindly older relative, and literally relating to an uncle.

clue.text: Furious before club possibly offers a chance to compete

indicators.note: before puts the word for furious first

parts.note: wild means furious, as in wild with anger
a club is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: An angry player goes to a club, hoping for a place in the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild card is an entry granted to a player who has not qualified, letting them take part.

clue.text: About to tuck into usual, I upset Marcus, say

indicators.note: to tuck into means the word for about goes inside the jumbled letters
upset means the letters of usual and I are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to tuck into their usual meal and annoys a friend called Marcus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the letters of usual and I, and 'to tuck into' sets the word for about inside them. Marcus Aurelius was a Roman emperor, so his name is defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus is the forename of the Roman emperor and Stoic philosopher Aurelius.

clue.text: Part of skeleton left, possessed by singular female?

indicators.note: possessed by means the letter for left is held inside the word for the female

parts.note: una is the feminine form of 'one' in Spanish and Italian, a single female

explanation.surface: A single woman owns a skeleton part that was left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: UNA, 'one' in feminine form in Spanish and Italian, holds L.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Oh — clue's construction is dubious

indicators.note: construction means the letters are built up again into a new word

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A solver exclaims that the way the clue is built is questionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' rearranges OH + CLUE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means disreputable, of shady character.

clue.text: Ought to accept responsibility for, with no sign of hesitation

indicators.note: with no means the hesitation sound is removed from the word

parts.note: to shoulder a burden is to accept responsibility for it
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone feels obliged to take on a duty without faltering.
explanation.definitionFit: Should expresses obligation, just like ought to.

clue.text: Excessive amount of fun, duetting?

indicators.note: amount of means a portion of the letters of fun duetting is taken

explanation.surface: A lot of fun singing in pairs proves too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means more than is warranted or appropriate.

clue.text: Endangered species state would raise

indicators.note: state means say out loud, so the word would is taken by its sound

parts.note: would said aloud sounds like wood
to cock is to raise, as a dog cocks its ear

explanation.surface: A government might lift protections for a creature at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' signals saying aloud: WOULD sounds like WOOD. The woodcock is a game bird whose numbers have fallen sharply in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcock is a wading bird now red-listed in the UK as in decline.

clue.text: Hear of a snag

explanation.surface: Someone learns about a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear it; a catch is a hidden drawback.

clue.text: A pound of tobacco?

explanation.surface: Someone buys a pound weight of tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is British slang for a pound sterling, not a pound weight; 'of' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A quid is slang for one pound sterling, and also a wad of chewing tobacco.

clue.text: Speak clearly, having some joints

explanation.surface: Someone with good joints talks distinctly.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate is to enunciate; articulate also means jointed, as an articulated lorry or limb.

clue.text: Back for some games

parts.note: in football and hockey a back is a player positioned to protect the goal

explanation.surface: Someone returns to play a few matches.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a back is a player in the rear line who guards the goal.

clue.text: Attention paid to your being unrefined

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Listening to someone reveals that they are coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and crude, lacking polish.
